task.requested_action: One white robotic arm with a black end effector remains stationary above the cardboard box; the other white robotic arm with a black end effector, positioned at the right side of the drawer and gripping its black handle, pulls the drawer fully open and then releases the handle.
task.target_description: an open refrigerator drawer filled with packaged frozen foods, its black handle, a cardboard box resting on the refrigerator surface to the left, and two white robotic arms with black end effectors
task.final_state_requirement: The refrigerator drawer is fully open; the arm that held the drawer handle has released the handle; the other arm remains stationary above the cardboard box.

requirement_checks.reason: The left white robotic arm with black end effector is above the brown cardboard box, but it does not remain stationary: from frame 0 to about frame 41 its end effector moves down into the box and lifts a packaged item, changing position rather than staying still above the box.

The right white robotic arm with black end effector is positioned at the right side of the drawer, moves toward the black drawer handle, and by the pulling phase its gripper is engaged with the black handle.

From frame 52 to frame 80, the right arm pulls the black handle outward and the drawer slides open, exposing progressively more packaged frozen foods; by frame 80 the drawer interior is widely visible in a fully open position relative to the enclosure.
After the drawer is pulled open, the right arm’s end effector remains attached to/holding the black handle through the final sampled frame 80; release of the handle is not observed.

observations.description: The left white robotic arm with black end effector is positioned over the brown cardboard box on the left. The right white robotic arm with black end effector moves from above the right drawer area toward the black handle on the drawer front and makes contact with the handle region by frame 21.

The left arm moves its end effector into the cardboard box and lifts a white-and-brown packaged item upward within the box; the package becomes more visible above the box contents as the arm raises it. The right arm remains at the drawer handle area.

The right arm pulls the black handle outward, and the drawer slides progressively open, exposing more packaged frozen foods inside. The left arm remains over the cardboard box holding the lifted package.

By the final sampled frames, the drawer is open with its interior widely visible, but the right arm’s end effector is still connected to the black handle and has not released it. The left arm remains above the cardboard box with the package held near/inside the box.

task_assessment.reason: Core progress is visible: the right arm approaches and grips the drawer handle, then pulls the drawer open to a clearly exposed interior by the end. However, the task is not complete because the left arm does not remain stationary above the box—it moves into the box and lifts a package—and the right arm does not release the handle by the final observed frame.

physics_assessment.reason: Within the sampled frames, the arms and drawer move in a causally understandable way: the right gripper contacts the handle, the drawer slides outward as the arm moves, and the left arm interacts with a package in the box. No confirmed interpenetration, impossible shape change, or unsupported floating is clearly visible; some motion blur and sampling gaps exist but do not by themselves prove a physical defect.

visual_assessment.reason: The scene, arms, box, drawer, handle, and packaged foods are generally identifiable, and the drawer opening is visible. Motion blur and reflections on the transparent surface slightly reduce fine detail, especially during arm movement, but they do not prevent judging the main positions and outcomes.

uncertainties: The exact moment the right gripper fully closes on the handle is partially obscured by motion blur and perspective.
The left gripper’s precise grasp on the package inside the box is not clearly resolved, so whether it is securely gripped or only contacted is somewhat uncertain.
Frames after 80 are not provided, so any release of the handle or further left-arm motion after the sampled segment cannot be verified.
